📊 Got it, Sherif — four facts, locked. Dispatching **CB** (product brief) in autonomous mode: no questions, I'll write it from what you've given me.

Workflow resolved — intent is **create**, fast path (no questions, per your instruction). Setting up the workspace now.

📊 Done, Sherif. The brief is written and polished.

**`_bmad/planning-artifacts/briefs/brief-scratch-project-2026-10-02/`**

| File | What's in it |
|---|---|
| `brief.md` | The brief — ~1.5 pages |
| `addendum.md` | Decision records (D1–D3) and the rejected SMS alternative, for whoever writes the PRD |
| `.memlog.md` | 14-entry audit trail of every decision and change |

### Your four facts, captured exactly

All four are stated verbatim in the brief, and I verified them byte-for-byte after the polish pass:

1. **Lantern** — given its own subsection as the double-booking guard, and carried into the addendum so the name survives into architecture.
2. **"A booking can be cancelled free of charge until 48 hours before it starts."**
3. **"The hall holds at most 60 people"** — fire-safety limit, **"the booking form must enforce it"**, and flagged as not user-configurable.
4. **Email over SMS, because the parish council has no budget for an SMS gateway** — stated with its reason attached, and recorded in the addendum as reversible-if-budget-changes rather than a settled preference.

### What I inferred, and flagged

You gave me four facts, not a discovery conversation, so everything else is inference and is tagged `[ASSUMPTION]` in-line. The brief ends with **7 open questions** those reduce to. Two are worth your attention now:

- **What happens to a cancellation inside the 48-hour window?** You told me what's free; you didn't tell me what isn't. A fee is the obvious answer but the costliest to build, since v1 has no payment handling.
- **Is "hall manager" a separate role from the parish council?** I wrote them as one stakeholder, inferred purely from the SMS budget line. If the keyholder is a distinct person with a part in the booking flow, that changes the scope.

The editorial pass (`bmad-review`, structure + prose lenses) caught both a real gap — three of my own assumptions were buried in body prose instead of listed with the others — and an inconsistency where I'd drifted between "keyholder" and "hall manager". Both fixed. I declined one finding: the lens wanted unspaced em dashes per Microsoft style, but spacing is consistent across both documents and changing it buys the reader nothing.

### Where this goes next

Answer those seven questions and this is ready for `bmad-prd` — the brief is shaped for that handoff. If you'd rather pressure-test the concept first, **WB** (the PRFAQ challenge) is the harder road. Or ask me to **validate** the brief once you've read it, and I'll critique it against its own purpose. `bmad-help` will also map the route for you any time.

📋 Morning, Sherif — John here, Product Manager.

I've got my bearings: `scratch-project`, and there's already a **product brief for Mossgate** sitting in your planning artifacts — a village hall booking page for three clubs, with two hard constraints (no double-booking, no capacity breach) and an addendum alongside it. Nice and tight in scope. No PRD yet.

A heads-up before we dig in: that brief has an `[ASSUMPTION]` flag on the current process — nobody confirmed how the three clubs coordinate today. That's exactly the kind of gap I'll keep poking at, because a PRD built on an unvalidated workflow assumption tends to ship the wrong increment.

You can call `bmad-help` any time if you want advice on where to go next.

Here's what I can do:

|---|------|-------------|--------|
| 1 | **PRD** | Create, update, or validate a PRD — state your intent or the skill will ask | `bmad-prd` |
| 2 | **CE** | Create the Epics and Stories Listing that will drive development | `bmad-create-epics-and-stories` |

Given there's a brief and no PRD, **option 1** is the obvious next step — but tell me what you want. Number, code, or just say it in your own words.


I've also got a research subagent out checking how comparable village-hall booking systems handle slot granularity, hirer identity, and late cancellations — it'll ground a couple of my guesses. That runs in the background.

**Working mode:** I'm taking **Fast path**, inferred from precedent — the brief run was explicitly no-discovery, and "pick up the work from here" reads as *proceed*, not *interview me*. Say the word if you'd rather walk the sections together.

But I won't draft on seven unanswered questions and call it a PRD. Here's the thing: your brief's open questions aren't evenly weighted. **Three of them block the FRs.** The other four I can carry as tagged assumptions without hurting anyone downstream.

### The three that block

**Q6 — Bookable hours and slot granularity.** This one's load-bearing in a way the brief understates. Lantern's entire job is "no two bookings in the same slot" — but *slot* is undefined, so Lantern is currently a guard over a thing with no shape. Arbitrary start/end times make Lantern an overlap-interval problem; fixed slots make it a uniqueness check. Different product, different build.
→ *My default:* **08:00–23:00, one-hour slots.** Clubs book contiguous runs (e.g. 19:00–21:00 = two slots).

**Q4 — Organiser identity, and who may cancel.** Can't write a booking FR without knowing who's holding the pen.
→ *My default:* **no self-signup.** The hall manager pre-registers a few named organisers per club; they sign in by emailed magic link. Three clubs is a fixed, tiny, known set — accounts with passwords are overhead for nobody's benefit. **Cancellation: any organiser of the booking's own club, plus the hall manager.** Club-level rather than person-level, so one organiser's holiday doesn't strand a booking.

**Q1 — Cancellation inside the 48-hour window.** Your addendum already reasons toward the answer: a fee is the most expensive option because payment handling is out of scope.
→ *My default:* **software refuses it and tells the organiser to contact the hall manager.** The booking stays on the record until a human removes it — which keeps the diary authoritative, the whole point of the product.

### The four I'll carry as assumptions

| Q | My assumption |
|---|---|
| **Q3** Club identities / standing | Three clubs, **equal standing, first-come-first-served.** No priority tiers. |
| **Q5** Hall manager a distinct role? | **Yes** — sees all bookings, can cancel any, is the escalation target for Q1. Parish council is an accountable stakeholder, *not* a system user. |
| **Q2** Current process | Not needed for the FRs. Affects migration and rollout, and I'll note it as exactly that. |
| **Q7** Email delivery target | I'd reframe rather than pick a number. Make **the page the authoritative record** and email a convenience, plus a *resend confirmation* action. Then you don't need a delivery-rate SLA you have no way to enforce on a parish budget. |

**What I need from you:** either "go" — and I draft on all of the above with every inference tagged `[ASSUMPTION]` — or correct the ones I've got wrong. Correcting Q6 matters most; the other two blockers I'm fairly confident on.

(Any point where you want to go deeper than Fast path allows, `bmad-advanced-elicitation` will push harder on a single section, and `bmad-party-mode` gets you Winston and Sally arguing with me about it.)

📋 Twelve entries in the memlog now. Here's what the research changed — I was wrong on one thing that matters.

### It reversed my Q6 recommendation

I proposed hourly slots. The sector evidence points the other way for exactly your case: halls with **regular club hirers** use **fixed named sessions** — Failand runs Morning 09:00–13:00 / Afternoon 13:30–17:30 / Evening 18:00–23:00 and explicitly refuses hourly hire; High Kelling the same shape.

And here's the detail I'd have missed entirely: **those gaps between sessions are deliberate.** 13:00→13:30, 17:30→18:00. That's changeover — one club clearing out while the next sets up. An hourly grid has no way to express it, so Lantern would happily sell 17:00–18:00 to one club and 18:00–19:00 to another with zero turnaround between a badminton net coming down and a toddler group arriving.

**Revised recommendation: three named sessions a day with changeover gaps.** It also makes Lantern dramatically simpler — a uniqueness check on (date, session) instead of interval-overlap arithmetic.
